newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo group signs agreement on Zambia mine.
newsitem.headline: Anglo group signs agreement on Zambia mine.

text.p: A consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it had signed a memorandum of understanding to conduct an exclusive feasibility study on the Konkola project in Zambia.

Anglo said in a statement the memorandum was signed on Tuesday by the consortium comprising its Zambian associate, Zambia Copper Investments Ltd, Gencor Ltd, Canada's Falconbridge Ltd, and the Zambian government and Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd.
"The MOU (memorandum of understanding) provides the consortium with the exclusive right to conduct a feasibility study on the Konkola project...," the statement said.

The consortium said it would also be prepared to assume ownership of the majority shareholding in a company called KonkCo -- which will include the existing assets and operations of ZCCM's Konkola division and Mufulira smelter and refinery -- in the second half of 1997 prior to a final decision on the project.
The Konkola Deep Mining Project (KDMP) includes the Konkola mine and concentrator and the Mufulira smelter and refinery.
"The KDMP ore resource contains 340 million tonnes at 3.8 percent copper and should sustain mining operations for more than 30 years," the statement said.
The consortium said a final commitment to assume ownership would be subject to the completion of a due diligence exercise on existing operations.

It would also be subject to agreement on a timetable for transferring ownership of the majority shares in KonkCo "which is consistent with the transfer of majority ownership to the successful bidder for the Nchanga and Nkana divisions in terms of the ZCCM privatisation process".

It would also be subject to agreement on the terms of a put and call mechanism that will allow the consortium to relinquish ownership of KonkCo at any time prior to a decision to proceed with the Konkola Deep project.
"ZCCM will be entitled in specific circumstances to call for the re-delivery of shares," the consortium statement said.

The consortium said the exclusive right to conduct a feasibility study on the project will terminate if it has not assumed majority ownership of KonkCo by June 30, 1997 or if later, the date when the Nchanga and Nkana divisions are privatised.
It said the due diligence exercise will be completed by mid-1997 and the feasibility study before the end of the year.
The Konkola Deep project is seen as the lifeline of the Zambian mining industry which has been in steady decline since the late 1980s.
